findings.description: Platform information gathering in setup.py for build configuration
findings.reasoning: This line calls platform.platform() to gather platform information for build configuration. This is in a setup.py file used during package installation/build time. The information is used locally to determine appropriate compiler flags for different platforms and is not exposed to users or logged. This is standard practice in Python setup.py files for cross-platform compatibility and does not constitute an information disclosure vulnerability in this context.

evidence.code_context:
The code is part of a setup.py build script that gathers platform information to configure compiler flags. The full context shows:

is_linux = sys.platform.startswith('linux') # could be linux or linux2
plat_platform = platform.platform()
plat_machine = platform.machine()
plat_compiler = platform.python_compiler()
try:
    # (sysname, nodename, release, version, machine)
    unam_machine = os.uname()[-1]
except AttributeError:
    unam_machine = ''

This information is used in conditional logic to set compiler flags like:
if (is_linux and plat_machine == "riscv64"):
    global_compile_args.append("-Os")

And:
if sys.platform == 'darwin' or 'clang' in plat_compiler:
    cpp_compile_args.append("--std=c++11")

This is build-time configuration, not runtime exposure.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: No dataflow to user-exposed sinks found. The platform information is only used locally for compiler flag decisions.
evidence.notes: This is a false positive because: 1) setup.py is a build script, not runtime code; 2) Platform info is standard for cross-platform builds; 3) No exposure to users; 4) No logging or output of this information.

findings.description: Platform information gathering in build script (not an information disclosure vulnerability)
findings.reasoning: This line calls platform.machine() to get the machine architecture. This is in a setup.py build script used to determine appropriate compiler flags for cross-platform compatibility. The information is used locally in conditional logic (lines 44-58) to set compiler flags like '-Os' for specific platforms. This is standard practice in Python build scripts and does not expose information to users or external systems. The information is not logged, printed, or transmitted anywhere. This is a false positive because it's build-time configuration, not runtime information disclosure.

evidence.code_context:
is_linux = sys.platform.startswith('linux') # could be linux or linux2
plat_platform = platform.platform()
plat_machine = platform.machine()
plat_compiler = platform.python_compiler()
try:
    # (sysname, nodename, release, version, machine)
    unam_machine = os.uname()[-1]
except AttributeError:
    unam_machine = ''
if (
       (sys.platform == "openbsd4" and unam_machine == "i386")
    or ("-with-redhat-3." in plat_platform and plat_machine == 'i686')
    or (sys.platform == "sunos5" and unam_machine == "sun4v") # SysV-based Solaris
    or ("SunOS" in plat_platform and plat_machine == "sun4v") # Old BSD-based SunOS
    or (is_linux and plat_machine == "ppc")
    # https://github.com/python-greenlet/greenlet/pull/300: When compiling for RISC-V the command
    # ``riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -pthread -fno-strict-aliasing -Wdate-time \
    #   -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -g -ffile-prefix-map=/build/python2.7-7GU7VT/python2.7-2.7.18=. \
    #   -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat -Werror=format-security -fPIC \
    #   -I/usr/include/python2.7
    #   -c src/greenlet/greenlet.cpp  -o build/temp.linux-riscv64-2.7/src/greenlet/greenlet.o``
    #
    # fails with:
    #
    # src/greenlet/platform/switch_riscv_unix.h:30:1: error: s0 cannot be used in 'asm' here
    #
    # Adding the -Os flag fixes the problem.
    or (is_linux and plat_machine == "riscv64")
):
    global_compile_args.append("-Os")
evidence.dataflow_analysis: No dataflow analysis performed as this is a local variable used only for build configuration.
evidence.notes: The plat_machine variable is used in conditional logic to determine if '-Os' compiler flag should be added for specific architectures (i686, ppc, riscv64). This is build-time configuration, not runtime information exposure.

plat_machine = platform.machine()
plat_compiler = platform.python_compiler()

    # (sysname, nodename, release, version, machine)
    unam_machine = os.uname()[-1]
except AttributeError:
    unam_machine = ''
if (

    or ("-with-redhat-3." in plat_platform and plat_machine == 'i686')
    or (sys.platform == "sunos5" and unam_machine == "sun4v") # SysV-based Solaris
    or ("SunOS" in plat_platform and plat_machine == "sun4v") # Old BSD-based SunOS
    or (is_linux and plat_machine == "ppc")
    # https://github.com/python-greenlet/greenlet/pull/300: When compiling for RISC-V the command
    # ``riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -pthread -fno-strict-aliasing -Wdate-time \
    #   -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -g -ffile-prefix-map=/build/python2.7-7GU7VT/python2.7-2.7.18=. \
    #   -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat -Werror=format-security -fPIC \
    #   -I/usr/include/python2.7
    #   -c src/greenlet/greenlet.cpp  -o build/temp.linux-riscv64-2.7/src/greenlet/greenlet.o``
    #
    # fails with:
    #
    # src/greenlet/platform/switch_riscv_unix.h:30:1: error: s0 cannot be used in 'asm' here
    #
    # Adding the -Os flag fixes the problem.
    or (is_linux and plat_machine == "riscv64")
):
    global_compile_args.append("-Os")

    # The clang compiler doesn't use --std=c++11 by default
    cpp_compile_args.append("--std=c++11")

evidence.notes: The plat_compiler variable is used later in the file to check if 'clang' is in the compiler string to add C++11 flag. This is build-time configuration, not runtime exposure.
